claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to understand your situation.

**First, let me ask about your child:**

How old is the child (or children) you're asking about? This is the first step in determining eligibility for Child Benefit.

- Is your child **under 16 years old**?
- Between **16-19 years old**?
- Or **20 years old or over**?

Please let me know your child's age so we can proceed with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. 

I have one child - Alex, who's 18 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, they fall into the **16-19 age category**. For children in this age group, eligibility depends on whether they're in approved education or training.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Here's the key question for Alex:**

Is Alex currently:
1. **In approved education or training** (such as A-levels, T-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQ Level 3 or below, or other approved courses)?
2. **Recently left education or training** (within the last 20 weeks)?
3. **Neither** - not in education/training and didn't recently leave?

Please let me know which situation applies to Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is currently in education - he's studying for his A-levels.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is studying for his A-levels, he's in approved education. Now I need to check that the education level meets the requirements for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! A-levels are approved non-advanced education for Child Benefit purposes. Now I need to check a few more details about Alex's education:

**1. Is Alex's course full-time?** (This means at least 12 hours per week of supervised study - which typical A-level courses are)

**2. Is this education funded by an employer or for a job already agreed with an employer?** (This would make Alex ineligible even if doing A-levels)

**3. Is Alex married or in a civil partnership?** (This can affect eligibility for 16-19 year olds unless they're financially dependent on you)

Please let me know about these details.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, it's a full-time A-level course at sixth form college - definitely more than 12 hours a week of study.

No, it's not funded by an employer or anything like that - just regular sixth form education.

And no, Alex isn't married or in a civil partnership.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Alex's A-level course meets all the education requirements:
- ✓ Full-time (12+ hours per week)
- ✓ Approved non-advanced education (A-levels)
- ✓ Not employer-funded
- ✓ Not married/in civil partnership

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

For 16-19 year olds in education, working 24 hours or more per week can affect Child Benefit eligibility. Please let me know about Alex's work situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's focused on his studies full-time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not working, so that requirement is met. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right?** Specifically:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Tax credits
- Income Support

Is Alex receiving any of these benefits in his own name?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name - no Universal Credit, ESA, or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex doesn't receive benefits in his own name. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Different types of apprenticeships have different rules:
- English apprenticeships (all types) disqualify from Child Benefit
- Scottish Modern Apprenticeships disqualify
- Welsh Foundation Apprenticeships are approved (but other Welsh apprenticeships disqualify)

Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't doing an apprenticeship - he's just doing A-levels at sixth form.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship, so that's fine. Now we need to check your eligibility as the claimant.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status:

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

If you normally live in the UK, that satisfies the residency requirement. 

Alternatively, there are other ways to meet the requirement if you:
- Have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Have pre-settled status with certain conditions (working, studying, sufficient resources, etc.)
- Are a Crown servant living abroad

Do you normally live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm based in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You meet the residency requirement as you normally live in the UK. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex:

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You mentioned Alex lives at home with you, which means you live with the child - this satisfies the responsibility requirement.

Just to confirm: **Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You're responsible for Alex as he lives with you. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about other potential claimants:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Anyone else

Or are you the only person claiming (or planning to claim) for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex - I'm the only one.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You're the only claimant for Alex. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Is Alex currently:**
- In hospital (for a continuous period)?
- In care (looked after by the local council)?
- Fostered?
- Or living normally at home with you?

Which situation applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living normally at home with me - not in hospital, care, or fostered.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex is living normally at home with you. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
One final question:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council providing financial support specifically for Alex's housing or upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Based on all the information you've provided, let me navigate to the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News - You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

Based on the comprehensive assessment, **you meet all the eligibility requirements** for Child Benefit for Alex.

### Why You're Eligible:

✅ **Alex qualifies as a child** - At 18 years old, studying full-time A-levels (approved non-advanced education with 12+ hours per week)
✅ **Not working full-time** - Alex is focused on studies
✅ **Not receiving benefits** - Alex doesn't claim ESA, Universal Credit, etc. in their own name
✅ **Not in an apprenticeship** - Just regular sixth form education
✅ **You meet residency requirements** - You live in the UK (Manchester)
✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - Alex lives at home with you
✅ **No competing claim** - You're the only person claiming for Alex
✅ **No council payments** - The council isn't paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Consider the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may have to pay a tax charge
5. **Payments** are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

You can apply here: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Do you have any questions about claiming or the High Income Child Benefit Charge?
